scenario: AITA For telling my Girlfriend she needs to quit whining about who eats what or I'll kick her out | Well, the title says it all, the past few weeks have both been really great and extremely infuriating. We don't live together, but we decided it would be best to stick together during these times as we have no family near as such she is staying with me as I have my own apartment and she has multiple roommates hence the choice. Well she eats more then any person I have ever known, especially considering her physical appearance, she is 5'4, petite, thin and yet she eats more than I do and I am 6'6 and a bit of a gymbro. To put it in to perspective, our food bill each week is roughly three times compared to what I usually spend alone. Yet she seems extremely selfconcious about this and as a result will act surprised when something is gone, try to blame me, states I am eating too much whenever I eat anything, essentially, she tries to deflect her eating habits and projects them on to me out of embarrassment about her eating so much I guess? The thing is, I don't care about her eating habits, she can eat whatever she wants to eat what I am done with is her constantly trying to blame me, whining about food and picking fights about it. I talked to her about it multiple times, argued with her about it multiple times but earlier today I just got so tired of another comment, this time brought on by me making a sandwhich at 2 PM when I had eaten at 10 AM I know right, horrible. So I told her that this crap was either going to stop right here and now or I'll kick her out and she can spend the coming weeks or months at her own place. She just started crying, called me horrible and locked herself in the bathroom. At this point I just dont get it anymore, am I being TA here or is she TA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the person in this situation is being toxic or not. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand everything. The person is a Muslim and is in a relationship with his girlfriend. They're not living together, but she's staying with him because they don't have family nearby. He has his own apartment, and she has multiple roommates, so they decided it's best for her to stay with him. The main issue seems to be about food. He says she eats more than anyone he's ever known, even though she's petite and thin. He's 6'6 and a gym bro, so he probably eats a lot too. He mentions that their weekly food bill is three times what he usually spends alone. He's frustrated because she acts surprised when something is gone, tries to blame him, says he's eating too much whenever he eats, and deflects her eating habits onto him. He doesn't care about her eating habits but is tired of her whining and blaming him. He's talked to her multiple times, argued about it, but today he snapped. He told her that either she stops whining about food or he'll kick her out. She started crying, called him horrible, and locked herself in the bathroom. Now he's confused about whether he's being toxic or if she is. Hmm, okay. So, first, I need to understand what "toxic" means in this context. Toxic behavior usually refers to actions that are harmful, manipulative, or controlling towards others. It can include things like emotional abuse, gaslighting, or creating an unhealthy environment. Looking at the situation, the girlfriend is eating more than he expects, which is causing financial strain. He's frustrated because she's deflecting her eating habits onto him, blaming him for things, and whining about it. He's tried talking to her about it, but it hasn't helped. Finally, he snapped and told her to stop or he'll kick her out. On one hand, he's trying to address a problem that's affecting their living situation. The increased food bill is a legitimate concern, especially if they're sharing expenses. He's frustrated because she's not taking responsibility for her actions and is instead blaming him. He's tried to communicate, but it hasn't worked, leading to him snapping. On the other hand, his reaction might be seen as controlling or threatening. Telling her to stop whining or else he'll kick her out could be seen as a form of emotional blackmail. It's a way of forcing her to change her behavior by threatening to end the relationship or make her leave. This kind of behavior can be toxic because it's manipulative and doesn't allow for healthy communication. Additionally, his reaction might be contributing to a cycle of conflict. If he's frustrated and she's upset, their arguments might be escalating without either of them addressing the underlying issues. Instead of finding a solution together, they're both reacting emotionally. I also need to consider cultural and personal contexts. As a Muslim, he might have certain values or expectations about relationships, such as respect, communication, and mutual support. If his actions are conflicting with these values, that could be another factor in determining whether he's being toxic. Another angle is to look at how both parties are handling the situation. She's deflecting her eating habits and blaming him, which might be a way of avoiding responsibility or dealing with her own feelings of guilt or embarrassment. He, in turn, is reacting with frustration and anger, which might be a way of dealing with his own stress about the financial impact. So, is he being toxic? Well, toxic behavior is about the impact of the actions on the other person. Threatening to kick her out if she doesn't stop whining is a form of control. It's not healthy communication because it's using fear to get her to change her behavior. Instead of working together to find a solution, he's trying to force her into submission. However, it's also important to recognize that he's feeling frustrated and overwhelmed. He's trying to manage a situation that's causing stress, and his reaction is a result of that. But the way he's handling it might not be the healthiest approach. In conclusion, while he has valid frustrations, the way he's expressing them by threatening to kick her out could be seen as toxic behavior because it's manipulative and doesn't foster a healthy, respectful relationship.
